Solve the following multiple-choice mathematics problem. You may reason before answering. End your final response with exactly "ANSWER: X", where X is one of A, B, C, D, E. Select one option.

a meeting has to be conducted with 6 managers . find the number of ways in which the managers may be selected from among 9 managers , if there are 2 managers who refuse to attend the meeting together .

A. 36
B. 40
C. 42
D. 45
E. 49

message.content:
9C6=84, exclude both together: 7C4=35, so 49.</think>Total ways: C(9,6)=84. Exclude selections containing both feuding managers: C(7,4)=35. So 84−35=49.

ANSWER: E

final_content:
Total ways: C(9,6)=84. Exclude selections containing both feuding managers: C(7,4)=35. So 84−35=49.

ANSWER: E
